notes:
ZMB (Investrust Bank) -- PRIORITY 1 RESOLVED AS NOT PRIVATE. The marketscreener directorate announcement (16 Apr 2015) confirms Dr Richard K. E. Chembe, previously in senior management at the Bank of Zambia and the IMF, was made Investrust managing director effective 1 May 2015 subject to Bank of Zambia approval, replacing Mr Friday Ndhlovu (retiring 31 May 2015); the announcement itself says nothing about ownership and describes Investrust only as 'the only listed indigenous Bank'. Ownership was then established from ZCCM-IH's own site: its 22 May 2018 release, which calls itself 'State owned ZCCM IH', says ZCCM-IH raised its holding in Investrust Bank Plc from 45.4% to 71.4% after a mandatory offer to minorities closed 30 April 2018 (https://www.zccm-ih.com.zm/2018/05/22/zccm-ih-ups-its-shares-in-investrust-bank/). A shareholder table reproduced at https://wiki.riteme.site/wiki/Investrust_Bank (as at 31 Dec 2016) also puts ZCCM Investments Holdings Plc at 71.4%, with Bank of Nevis International, the Workers' Compensation Fund Control Board (a statutory body) and the Stanbic Bank Zambia Pension Scheme behind it; that table is internally inconsistent (percentages sum to ~113%), so the ZCCM-IH release is the reliable figure. Conclusion: at the time of Chembe's 2015 appointment the Zambian state mining holding company was already Investrust's largest shareholder (45.4%), rising to a controlling 71.4%. Investrust is therefore substantially state-owned and the move is filed as a public move, NOT as a move through private finance. ZMB is not closed by this.

KOR (Seoul Foreign Exchange Brokerage) -- PRIORITY 1 STILL HELD, two facts still missing. The Asiae English article confirms Seoul Foreign Exchange Brokerage announced 'on the 2nd' that an extraordinary general meeting of shareholders appointed Jeong Gyu-il, former Deputy Governor of the Bank of Korea, as CEO and President, and that he joined the Bank of Korea in 1987 and held senior Bank of Korea roles including international cooperation, economic statistics and deputy governor. (1) THE YEAR IS NOT IN THE TEXT. The article says only 'on the 2nd'. The URL slug (2021070215182015950) and the search index imply 2 July 2021, but no sentence on the page states a year for the appointment, so I did not put a year on a record. The Korean original at https://www.asiae.co.kr/article/2021070215182015950 is robots-disallowed to WebFetch and would show a dated byline -- THIS ONE URL NEEDS A HAND CHECK, and a human reading the byline date would close KOR. (2) OWNERSHIP NOT FOUND. The company's English legal name is 'Seoul Money Brokerage Services, Ltd.' (established from its GLEIF/Bloomberg LEI record 98840007LEN5VMRVQX37, which gives the Korean name Seoul Foreign Exchange Brokerage Co Ltd, a Jung-gu Seoul address, and 'Parent Information Not Provided / NON_CONSOLIDATING' for both direct and ultimate parent, so the LEI record names no owner). Four searches in English and Korean for its shareholders returned nothing that states them -- the hits were all about FX market policy, or about the other broker, Korea Money Brokerage (kmbco.com). Per the rules I am NOT filing this: silence about ownership is not evidence that the brokerage is private. What is needed is a shareholder list for Seoul Money Brokerage Services (likely in a DART filing or on its own corporate site) plus the byline date.

BLZ (Central Bank of Belize) -- CLOSED, and with the bank's own words. The Board of Directors page (https://www.centralbank.org.bz/board-of-directors) is names and titles only, no biographies at all. But the Office of the Governor sub-page carries full dated careers for the Governor and both Deputy Governors, and Deputy Governor Marina Laetitia Murillo's says she left the Bank and from 1998 worked in project management in the non-government sector and in management positions in the PRIVATE FINANCIAL SECTOR, returning to the Bank in November 2011 -- the employers are not named, which the rules permit. Filed. Two other Belize careers from the same page were NOT filed: Governor Kareem Michael resigned from the Bank in 2014 to be Senior Business Analyst at Belize Electricity Limited and returned as Deputy Governor in November 2017 -- an electric utility is not finance, so it goes here and not into records; Deputy Governor Hollis Parham's career since February 1984 is entirely inside the Bank.

MNG (Bank of Mongolia) -- CLOSED. Last round's route was wrong: it is Mongolbank, not the hiring firm, that publishes the dated careers, on per-person profile pages (mongolbank.mn/en/profile/NNNN) rather than on the board page. The board-of-directors page itself (https://www.mongolbank.mn/en/p/board-of-directors) lists eight officers with photos and no biography text. Profile 8766 gives a Supervisory Board member whose career is thirteen years at Golomt Bank (2006 teller through 2018-2019 project director), then MIG LLC and BPM Mongolia LLC, then the Bank of Mongolia's Supervisory Board from 2025 -- filed. Golomt Bank's ownership is stated on its own About Us page: 'Golomt Bank was established on March 6, 1995 as a subsidiary company of Bodi International LLC', with an IPO in 2022 making it a joint-stock company (https://www.golomtbank.com/en/about-us) -- a private limited company's subsidiary, now exchange-listed, with no state shareholder named, so a private commercial bank. NOTE A PAGE DEFECT: profile 8766's body text names Mr KHOSJARGAL Undraa while the page metadata carries the name from profile 8763 (Mr TELMEN Gerelt); I have keyed the record to the body text and named the person accordingly, but a hand check of that page would be worth one minute. Profile 8763 (Telmen Gerelt) is Mongol Post JSC, Ard Credit JSC, MEC Partners LLC, LG International and Samsung C&T -- Ard Credit is the only financial one and the page does not say what it is or who owns it, so not filed. Profile 8764 (Enkhjargal Danzanbaljir) is a full dated career but every outside employer is public (State Bank of Mongolia, the intergovernmental International Investment Bank, World Bank, ADB, AIIB, Millennium Challenge Corporation, GIZ/EU) -- filed as a public move only.

MKD (National Bank of the Republic of North Macedonia) -- NOT CLOSED, and I am reporting rather than filing, because of the industry question. The three per-person CV paths you gave all failed through WebFetch as well as curl (client_error on www.nbrm.mk/ana-mitreska-biografija-en.nspx, .../emilija-nacevska-biografija-en.nspx, .../fadil-bajrami-biografija-en.nspx, both plain and with :443), so the per-path Cloudflare block covers them. One alternate path DID read: https://nbrm.mk/ns-newsarticle-cv_fadil_bajrami.nspx, the bank's own CV of Vice Governor Fadil Bajrami. It states he spent 'more than five years in managerial positions in the private sector', was mayor of the Municipality of Oslomej, was an MP 1999-2005 (chairing the Economic Policy and Development Committee and sitting on banking and commerce committees), was Vice Governor from September 2005 to September 2012 and was re-appointed Vice Governor by Parliament in July 2012, and has lectured at the State University in Tetovo since 2011. So there IS a stated private-sector move into the central bank with the firm withheld -- but the page withholds the INDUSTRY too and gives no dates for it, and your rules say a private move that is not shown to be financial must not be filed with public_move false. YOUR CALL: if 'private sector, industry unstated' is admissible to you, that one sentence closes MKD, and the URL above is the citation. Also unread and still worth a call: https://www.nbrm.mk/ns-newsarticle-emilija-nacevska-i-ana-mitreska-se-imenuvani-za-viceguverneri-na-nbrm-en.nspx (appointment announcement for the two vice governors, may carry their CVs) and https://www.nbrm.mk/izvrshen-odbor-en.nspx (Executive Board) -- both appeared in search but the first failed client_error; the second was not fetched for want of budget.

GUY (Bank of Guyana) -- NOT CLOSED. Took the hiring-firm route as instructed: Republic Bank (Guyana) Limited is the largest private commercial bank there and publishes a full executive-team and board page, https://republicguyana.com/about/executive-team. I read every profile on it. NOT ONE mentions the Bank of Guyana or any other central bank. The outside employers named are the Republic Financial Holdings group, the Caribbean Development Bank, NBIC, Label House Group, Caribbean Airlines, ATNI, GTT, the Massy Group, Nadir Nadir & Seepersaud, Carib Hibiscus Development and Florida Export Finance Corporation. What is missing for Guyana is a biography of a named former Bank of Guyana governor or deputy governor (e.g. Gobind Ganga, Lawrence Williams) published by whichever firm hired them; the untried firms are Demerara Bank, GBTI and the local insurers, plus the Guyana Association of Bankers.

SLE (Bank of Sierra Leone) -- NOT CLOSED. The richest biography available for a Bank of Sierra Leone principal is the George Washington University Africa Finance and Trade profile of Governor Ibrahim L. Stevens, https://africafinancetrade.gwu.edu/node/281. It is a full career and it is entirely public: about a decade at the Bank of England including the Centre for Central Banking Studies, secondment from the Bank of England to be the Bank of Sierra Leone's Director of Research 2008-2010, Country Programme Director at the LSE's International Growth Centre, macroeconomic adviser to Rwanda's Ministry of Finance, head of a GIZ-funded project, then Deputy Governor from July 2014 (reappointed 2019), First Deputy Governor after the Bank of Sierra Leone Act 2019, and Governor since November 2023. Filed as a public move only. No private financial employer appears anywhere in it. Unread and cheap next time: https://bsl.gov.sl/Management.html (senior management, may give prior employers where the board page gave only dates).

COL (Banco de la Republica) -- NO CALL SPENT THIS ROUND, as the central bank side was exhausted last round and the hiring-firm route needs a name-by-name search I could not fit in budget. Untried: Grupo Bancolombia, Banco de Bogota, Corficolombiana, Fiduciaria Bancolombia and the brokerage houses, searched against named former co-directors and technical deputy governors (e.g. Carolina Soto Losada, Gerardo Hernandez, Juan Pablo Zarate, Hernando Vargas).

MOZ (Banco de Mocambique) -- NO CALL SPENT THIS ROUND for the same reason. Last round's Millennium bim executive pages never mention the central bank. Untried hiring firms: Standard Bank Mocambique, Absa Bank Mocambique, Banco Comercial e de Investimentos (BCI), and the insurers, searched against named former governors and deputy governors (e.g. Ernesto Gove, Waldemar de Sousa, Joana Matsombe, Victor Gomes).

DOM (Dominican Republic) -- one search spent, no biography found. The hits were news of Hector Valdez Albizu's ratifications and his 50 years at the BCRD, plus Grupo Popular's own executive reshuffles, none of which states a move between the central bank and a private firm. The route that should work next time is the BCRD's own 'Miembros de la Junta Monetaria' page and the Asociacion de Bancos Multiples (ABA) board page.

UNTOUCHED FOR WANT OF BUDGET, no call spent, nothing learned: BOL, ECU, GMB, NIC, KHM, LAO, MMR, BRN, TON.

TOOL NOTE FOR THE NEXT ROUND: curl was refused by the permission classifier in this environment ('Unauthorized Access'), so the cheap curl+pdftotext route was unavailable and every page cost a WebFetch. Plan the budget accordingly. Two PDFs I therefore could not read: https://nbrm.mk/WBStorage/Files/ManBodiesOfTheNationalBank.pdf (failed client_error on WebFetch too) and https://bsl.gov.sl/Approved%20Organogram.pdf.

records.people: Marina Laetitia Murillo (Deputy Governor, Monetary and Financial Systems)
records.move: from management positions in the private financial sector (employers not named) back to the Central Bank of Belize as Economist I
records.summary: The Central Bank of Belize's own Office of the Governor page states that Marina Laetitia Murillo began at the Bank as a Research Officer in August 1991, that from 1998 she worked in project management in the non-government sector and in management positions in the private financial sector, and that she returned to the Bank in November 2011 as Economist I, rising to Assistant Manager of the Financial System Development Unit in October 2018 and to Deputy Governor effective 1 September 2022; the outside employers are financial and the page itself characterises them as private, so the private-finance fact comes from the central bank's own published biography rather than from any inference, though the firms are not named.
records.source_title: The Governor - Office of the Governor, Central Bank of Belize

records.people: Khosjargal Undraa (Member of the Supervisory Board)
records.move: from thirteen years at Golomt Bank, then MIG LLC and BPM Mongolia LLC, to Member of the Supervisory Board of the Bank of Mongolia
records.summary: The Bank of Mongolia's own profile page gives Khosjargal Undraa's dated career as branch teller, loan officer and business centre staff at Golomt Bank from 2006 to 2007, product development manager there 2007-2010, branch director 2010-2014, director of channel management 2014-2018 and project director of its business process re-engineering project 2018-2019, then deputy director of MIG LLC 2021-2022 and chief executive of BPM Mongolia LLC from 2022, before joining the central bank's Supervisory Board in 2025; Golomt Bank is a private commercial bank, a fact taken from the bank's own About Us page, which states it was established on 6 March 1995 as a subsidiary company of Bodi International LLC and became a joint-stock company at its 2022 IPO, naming no state shareholder.
records.source_title: Khosjargal Undraa, Member of the Supervisory Board - Bank of Mongolia profile

records.people: Enkhjargal Danzanbaljir (Deputy Governor 2007-2010; Member of the Supervisory Board since 2025)
records.move: from Deputy Governor and London representative of the Bank of Mongolia out to the Asian Development Bank, World Bank, AIIB, the International Investment Bank and the state-owned State Bank of Mongolia, and back to the Bank of Mongolia's Supervisory Board
records.summary: The Bank of Mongolia's own profile page gives Enkhjargal Danzanbaljir's dated career as chief economist and adviser to the Governor 2001-2002, resident representative in London 2002-2007, Deputy Governor 2007-2010 and director of the London representative office 2010-2013, then finance and banking adviser at the Asian Development Bank from December 2010, a role at the AIIB in 2015, World Bank consultant in 2016, senior adviser to an EU and GIZ project 2017-2018, Mongolia's director on the board of the intergovernmental International Investment Bank 2021-2022, interim chief executive of Millennium Challenge Corporation Mongolia 2022-2023 and independent board member of the State Bank of Mongolia 2020-2024, before rejoining the central bank's Supervisory Board in 2025; every outside employer named is a multilateral body, a state-owned bank or a donor programme, so no private firm appears and this is recorded as a public move.
records.source_title: Enkhjargal Danzanbaljir, Member of the Supervisory Board - Bank of Mongolia profile

records.people: Dr Richard K. E. Chembe (senior management, Bank of Zambia)
records.move: from senior management positions at the Bank of Zambia and the IMF to Managing Director of Investrust Bank Plc, effective 1 May 2015
records.summary: Investrust Bank Plc's directorate announcement of 16 April 2015 states that Dr Richard K. E. Chembe, who held senior management positions at the Bank of Zambia and the International Monetary Fund and was special assistant for economic and development affairs to Zambia's fourth president, was appointed managing director effective 1 May 2015 subject to Bank of Zambia approval, replacing Mr Friday Ndhlovu who was to retire on 31 May 2015; the hiring employer is NOT private, because ZCCM Investments Holdings Plc, which its own 22 May 2018 release describes as 'State owned ZCCM IH', raised its Investrust stake from 45.4% to 71.4% that year, meaning the Zambian state mining holding company was already the bank's largest shareholder when Chembe was appointed, so this is recorded as a public move and does not evidence a move through private finance.
records.source_title: Investrust Bank PLC Announces Directorate Changes

records.people: Dr Ibrahim L. Stevens (Governor; previously Deputy Governor and Director of Research)
records.move: from about a decade at the Bank of England, on secondment, to Director of Research at the Bank of Sierra Leone 2008-2010 ; from the London School of Economics International Growth Centre and macroeconomic advisory work for Rwanda's Ministry of Finance to Deputy Governor of the Bank of Sierra Leone in July 2014
records.summary: The George Washington University Africa Finance and Trade profile of Dr Ibrahim L. Stevens states that he spent about a decade at the Bank of England working on financial stability and monetary analysis and as senior adviser at its Centre for Central Banking Studies, served as Director of Research at the Bank of Sierra Leone from 2008 to 2010 on secondment from the Bank of England, was Country Programme Director at the London School of Economics International Growth Centre, macroeconomic adviser to Rwanda's Ministry of Finance and Economic Development and head of a German International Cooperation funded project, was appointed Deputy Governor in July 2014 and reappointed for a second five-year term in 2019, became First Deputy Governor under the Bank of Sierra Leone Act 2019 and has been Governor since November 2023; every outside employer named is a central bank, a ministry, a university programme or a donor agency, so no private firm is involved and this is recorded as a public move.
records.source_title: Ibrahim L. Stevens - GWU Africa Finance and Trade Initiative
